question: Which focus and navigation guarantees must hold for voids, owned controls, inactive editors and read-only views?
method: best-api-review/history-v3; second-failed-fix recovery; redesign-from-first-principles hard-cut comparison
trigger: TaskHub #46 reporter contradiction against pushed commit 4183236efe: synchronously restoring the Editable around projected-selection removeAllRanges still leaves the real browser editor unfocused while stale focus state permits the floating toolbar to open.
requirements: An expanded projected selection must preserve the exact Editable as the browser keyboard focus owner without a later focus call, timer or copied-UI repair.

The browser selection must retain a collapsed editable caret while Plite paints the expanded projected selection, so the browser has one live input position without duplicate expanded-selection paint.
Plite focus state and toolbar visibility may follow the browser focus owner; they must not substitute for or mask a missing browser caret.
Retained-fragment identity and projected command targeting remain private mounted-view state and must not be flattened into document truth.
A real external focus target must still win, and inactive selection remains the intentional representation only after a genuine focus transfer.
evidenceReuse: Retains the 2026-09-12 exact-view focus, native input and projected-selection ownership split and the 2026-09-25 rejection of toolbar-owned focus, parallel focus state and a public projected-selection API. Reopens only the previously selected removeAllRanges focus-restoration mechanism after the reporter contradicted its pushed implementation. Current source shows expanded projected selection export makes the browser Selection empty while hiding the caret, applyEditableBlur suppresses focus truth updates during isUpdatingSelection, and focusPliteEditable focuses an expanded view selection without installing a native caret.
summary: Pursue replacing the empty browser Selection state with a collapsed native caret resolved by the existing projected-selection owner. Delete the removeAllRanges focus-restoration wrapper; keep projected paint and command targeting private, and keep the toolbar as a focus-gated geometry consumer.

reconciliation.question: Which focus and navigation guarantees must hold for voids, owned controls, inactive editors and read-only views?
reconciliation.reason: The exact Editable, projected selection and copied UI remain separate owners; no public API, toolbar focus call, timer or parallel focus state is justified.

reconciliation.question: Which focus and navigation guarantees must hold for voids, owned controls, inactive editors and read-only views?
reconciliation.reason: The selected synchronous restore after removeAllRanges failed in the reporter browser and preserves an empty native selection state whose later blur can be hidden by isUpdatingSelection.

alternatives: Keep removeAllRanges plus synchronous, microtask, frame or timeout focus restoration: rejected because the browser selection remains empty, external focus races multiply, and the pushed synchronous variant already failed.

Close the floating toolbar when inactive-selection paint is present or add another focus flag: rejected because it hides the symptom while leaving keyboard ownership broken and duplicates focus truth.
Keep the expanded native range alongside projected paint: rejected because it creates two expanded visual selections and cannot represent retained-fragment semantics as one native range.

Move repair into the toolbar, inactive-selection coordinator or React context: rejected because those are consumers of exact-view focus and cannot create a browser editing caret without cross-layer compensation.

Delete projected selection and flatten retained fragments into the model selection: rejected because retained identity, authored-view coordinates and multi-segment command targets are current hard jobs.

Export an expanded projected selection as a collapsed native caret at an existing writable projected target while projected decorations own expanded paint: chosen because it removes the empty-selection state and reuses the exact mounted selection owner without a public primitive.
proofLimits: This review selects the repair owner and invariant from current source plus the reporter contradiction. Per the user's latest instruction, no real-browser proof is run or claimed in this repair turn; browser acceptance remains delegated to the user. Static and focused non-browser checks can reject type and selection-contract errors but cannot certify native focus, caret paint or first-key routing.
